page_title: AI Testing Platform | API, Unit & Integration Testing - Tusk

summary.name: Tusk
summary.one_liner: Tusk is an AI testing platform that generates and maintains API, unit, and integration tests for code changes, surfacing them in pull requests.
use_cases: Generating unit tests for pull requests
Raising test coverage on legacy codebases
Maintaining existing test suites after code changes
Adding AI-written tests to CI/CD pipelines
summary.what_it_does: Tusk uses live traffic and business context to generate test cases aimed at catching real-world regressions, and the page claims this catches regressions in 43% of PRs. It runs as a CLI that is set up with a single command and adds generated tests locally or to an existing branch. It self-iterates on tests that error when run, and automatically maintains existing test suites on each commit to reflect current business logic. It also enforces test coverage and code quality requirements on pull requests, shown as a CI check that adds tests to a PR.
notable: Self-healing tests that update existing suites on every commit
Self-iterates on failing generated tests without copilot back-and-forth
Posts generated tests as a commit/check on pull requests
Customer quotes cite large coverage gains, such as 2,500 to 7,000+ tests in a month
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page
The 43% regression-catch figure is a vendor claim with no methodology given
